top3.whyItMatters: Model leadership is shifting fast; avoid locking contracts to one provider.

top3.headline: OpenAI tightens GPT-6.2 limits; Astra users hit caps 40% faster
top3.whyItMatters: AI seat value can change without notice; budget with headroom and a backup vendor.

top3.headline: Hermes Agent gets an official Obsidian connector for local shared memory
top3.whyItMatters: Agents that read your own notes locally cut privacy risk in knowledge work.

items.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-6.2 usage: Astra hits limits 40% faster
items.takeaway: Per the linked post by thsottiaux, Sol limits also arrive 25% sooner; the HN thread drew 424 points.
items.soWhat: Seat plans can shrink overnight; track real usage per team before committing to one vendor.

items.title: MengTo open-sources three.js skills behind a GPT-6.2 Astra build
items.takeaway: He built an endless motorcycle ride with parallax and fisheye camera tricks, and shared the skills on GitHub.
items.soWhat: Reusable skill files let design teams hand agents proven visual techniques instead of starting from scratch.

items.title: Hermes Agent can now run an Obsidian vault as shared memory
items.takeaway: NousResearch shipped an official connector; notes stay local.
items.soWhat: Local knowledge bases give agents context without sending your notes to a vendor's cloud.

items.title: Ruben Hassid builds a full presentation from one Claude Opus prompt
items.takeaway: He selects Opus 5.5 on High, pastes one prompt asking for graphics and transitions, and adds nothing else.
items.soWhat: First drafts of decks now take one prompt; the editing is where your team adds value.

items.title: Gemini Neon usage on Perplexity doubled in a day, past 100B tokens
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas says this came with no default model routing; harness changes fixed formatting issues.
items.soWhat: Users are choosing Google's model on their own; revisit model defaults in your AI stack.

items.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan for up to 1 million data center satellites
items.takeaway: The Verge reports the FCC signed off on SpaceX's plan to put data centers into orbit.
items.soWhat: Compute supply may move to orbit; watch who controls that capacity when planning long-term AI costs.
